domain.notes: Starter template — insurance claims, US (USD / MDY / SSN-EIN-routing-ZIP validators derive from country)

datasets.name: Claims register
datasets.description: One row per claim: claimed incident date/site, damage photos, repair invoice. Photo capture time + GPS are screened against the claimed incident automatically (EXIF-vs-claim).

columns.name: payout_account
columns.description: Payout bank account — the ring/double-dip key

columns.name: payout_routing
columns.description: Payout ABA routing number — checksum-validated automatically under the US locale pack

columns.name: incident_date
columns.description: Claimed incident date — photos captured BEFORE this cannot show the incident

columns.name: policy_start
columns.description: Policy start (denormalized onto the claim) — claim-within-days-of-policy-start is the classic opportunistic-fraud date rule

columns.name: damage_photo_url
columns.description: Damage photo — reuse across claims is a double-dip signal; EXIF screened vs the claim

columns.name: claimant_id_url
columns.description: ID scan — ROLE identity: reuse by the SAME claimant is verification, never a flag

columns.name: repair_invoice_url
columns.description: Repair invoice — line items are arithmetic-checked; content near-dups caught across claims; the estimate reference on it verifies against surveyor_estimates (verify_against below)

columns.name: policy_tnc_url
columns.description: Policy T&C copy. ROLE supporting = never fingerprinted (its reuse is meaningless).

verify_against.name: invoice_vs_surveyor_estimate
verify_against.description: the repair invoice cites the surveyor estimate it bills against — a missing estimate or an inflated total vs the approved amount is the repair-bill-divergence tell (claims-pack tolerances apply)

datasets.name: Surveyor estimates
datasets.description: Approved surveyor damage estimates, estimate-number-keyed — the system of record repair invoices verify against. No fraud_screening block: silence means this dataset is never screened itself; it is a verification TARGET.

datasets.name: Empanelled garages
datasets.description: Reference list of empanelled garages. EXPLICIT OPT-OUT example (applies:false) — but note: declaring garage identifiers in the CLAIMS dataset's identity_fields is what catches garage rings; the master itself needs no screening.

datasets.name: Policy master
datasets.description: Active policies with start dates — claim-within-days-of-policy-start is the classic opportunistic-fraud date rule (E6, declarative date rules).

sources.name: Industry fraud registry — VIN/claim lookup (API-as-dataset)
sources.description: Live industry fraud-registry passthrough (IIB/ClaimSearch-style), exposed as a parameterised dataset: the agent queries it with the case's identifiers and nests raw matches under external_registry_matches in the fraud signals (scored as the highest-precision signal). The MCP holds the corporate credentials + FCRA-grade audit. TEMPLATE — replace base_url/path/mapping with the real registry contract.

datasets.name: Prior claims by VIN
datasets.description: Industry-wide prior claims for a VIN. NOTE: a rest dataset is an agent-read lookup and registry-evidence source — it can NOT be a payment_proof/verify_against target (the structured read-by-key plane covers sql/odata/soql/mongodb only).
